E2.evidence: Step 1: the reporter's chainable controller plugin (four_wheel_steering::OdometryProvider in libodometry_provider.so, package drive_controller, built in the reporter's workspace) and its host framework ros2_control (controller_interface / hardware_interface, installed from /opt/ros/jazzy) are separate units (a plugin and its host framework). Step 2: the key under which the framework stores the plugin's exported state interfaces crosses the boundary; the plugin indexes the framework-owned map exported_state_interfaces_ with a key in the older convention. PR #2038 (465e5d02) changed the provider from "const auto interface_name = state_interface->get_interface_name();" to "const auto interface_name = state_interface->get_name();" before "exported_state_interfaces_.insert({interface_name, state_interface});". A consumer using the full name works (the reporter's resolution), so it does not occur with any correct peer. Step 3/4/5: no deployment rename, build, or firmware change.

failed_conditions.quote: The ``exported_state_interfaces_`` and ``exported_reference_interfaces_`` now uses the the full interface name as the key to the unordered_map, instead of the interface type. This is related to (`#2038 <https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/pull/2038>`_). For instance, the key would be ``joint_1/position`` instead of ``position``.

loudness_evidence: The mismatch surfaces only as a runtime crash in the controller update, with no build, load, or activation diagnostic: "[ros2_control_node-2] Segmentation fault (Address not mapped to object [0x80])" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/2121).

resolution.summary: The consumer indexes exported_state_interfaces_ with the full interface name ("<controller name>/<interface name>") instead of the bare interface name; the provider keeps the new key convention and documents it in the migration notes (PR #2129, documentation only).
resolution.evidence: Reporter, same installation: "Hey, never mind. \nThe issue is solved, it was the interface_name being incomplete. I did not add the node name to it." (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/2121#issuecomment-2747169475). The provider in the working composition is the unchanged Jazzy install (4.27.0, inferred as for the broken composition); the consumer is the reporter's edited, unpublished controller (label as-reported-2025-03-24, no code quoted).

notes: The same key change applies to exported_reference_interfaces_ (not used by the reporter). consumer_built_against is inferred: the reporter's unprefixed key matches the provider's declarations up to the parent of 465e5d02 (c302212822acc735cdb6dd2ab67d4e967c201bcf); 4.26.0 (e574645f, 2025-02-07) is the last release before that commit and the plausible pre-update Jazzy binary ("before the last update it worked"), but an earlier Jazzy release cannot be excluded. The consumer was compiled against 4.27.0 headers (the trace shows the templated set_value<double> introduced after 4.26.0) while its source still uses the pre-465e5d02 key convention. Class choice: the map member's declaration is unchanged (std::unordered_map<std::string, hardware_interface::StateInterface::SharedPtr>); what changed is the convention for the key string, so representation_convention is used; from the consumer's view the entry it looks up is effectively renamed, so element_removed_or_renamed is an alternative reading. The crash mechanism (operator[] default-inserting an entry whose set_value dereferences a null handle) is inferred from the trace and not stated in the source. Resolution status 'observed' rests on the reporter's statement; the consumer's resolved revision is only an as-reported label with an empty artifact section, so an adjudicator applying the revision-identification requirement strictly could downgrade it to 'recommended'.
